pr_title: lightning: sample files and pre-allocate rowID before restoring chunk
pr_body:
<!--

### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

Please create an issue first to describe the problem.

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and 
linking the relevant issues via the "close" or "ref".

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: close #28776 

Problem Summary:

Currently, Lightning pre-allocates rowIDs for each row when populating chunks according to data file sizes. But it occurs that estimates of rowID are now conservatively too large so that Lightning usually pre-allocates a large number of rowIDs, which significantly exceeds what we need. This issue may result in:
1. if the number of rows is relatively close to the maximum of the data type of its `auto_increment` field, Lightning is likely to allocate rowIDs that exceed this limit. (e.g. `2^31` rows of data may probably have `2^32` rowIDs, which exceeds the range of `int32` if the `auto_increment` field is `int32`)
2. Too much space of rowID is wasted because of over-estimate.

### What is changed and how it works?
In this pr, I'm about to:
1. sample rows from data files and do a better estimation.
2. re-allocate ids when they are run out (due to bad estimation)
3. early stop when the rowID overflows

issue_context.title: [lightning] Estimate rowid might overflow when import data and auto fill int column.
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)
This issue was created according to ONCALL-3504

Using lightning to import data, before lightning import, create the schema in TiDB manually and adding an extra column: `id_auto_incr` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT, during import, lightning will estimate the rowid and auto fill this column (as this column doesn't exists in data source), and rowid might overflow in some cases and result in data inconsistency.



### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)
Lightning import should be successful and data consistency should be ensured.

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)
Lighting import failed with checksum mistch.

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)
Lightning: 4.0.14
comments: @kennytm What do you think, seems do this check in precheck is not easy? Can we only check in `chunkRestore`?🤔
given that we have max-error now i think we should turn the default SQL mode back to `strict_trans_table` to catch the 32-bit overflow.

There are other issues when filling `auto_increment` field with lightning.

test: 
- source `csv` file: 312535480 rows with only **one** column `a` ranging from 0~312535479.
- create table with `auto_increment` id
- lightning restore

result:
```
mysql> select count(*) from test use index(id);
+-----------+
| count(*)  |
+-----------+
| 312535480 |
+-----------+
1 row in set (15.22 sec)

mysql> select count(*) from test;
+-----------+
| count(*)  |
+-----------+
| 312535480 |
+-----------+
1 row in set (15.06 sec)

mysql> select * from test order by id asc limit 10;
+----+---+
| id | a |
+----+---+
|  1 | 0 |
|  2 | 1 |
|  3 | 2 |
|  4 | 3 |
|  5 | 4 |
|  6 | 5 |
|  7 | 6 |
|  8 | 7 |
|  9 | 8 |
| 10 | 9 |
+----+---+
10 rows in set (0.01 sec)

mysql> select * from test order by id desc limit 10;
+------------+-----------+
| id         | a         |
+------------+-----------+
| 1651778746 | 312535479 |
| 1651778745 | 312535478 |
| 1651778744 | 312535477 |
| 1651778743 | 312535476 |
| 1651778742 | 312535475 |
| 1651778741 | 312535474 |
| 1651778740 | 312535473 |
| 1651778739 | 312535472 |
| 1651778738 | 312535471 |
| 1651778737 | 312535470 |
+------------+-----------+
10 rows in set (0.01 sec)
```
id didn't overflow. But we were expecting `id == a+1` but got `165177874*`. I guess both originated from the same bugs of Lightning.

Possible root cause:
Lightning evaluates the data file's size and infers `PrevRowMax` and `RowIDMax` for each chunk. The `PrevRowMax` is assigned to `parser.lastRow.rowID` before reading and parsing the data file. 

After reading a row from the file, `parser.lastRow` is set this row, with `rowID = parser.lastRow.rowID++`. However, since `PrevRowMax` is an estimate, it obviously doesn't strictly equal the true rowID, and thus, we may have id much larger than what we expected.

Similarly, when `PrevRowMax` is over-estimated (e.g. overflows int(32)), we may probably make id exceeding the maximum of int.

It's intuitive to add a check or re-estimate these values, but would it be better to have a global ID allocator managing these stuff for us? /cc @gozssky @niubell

> this issue affects 4.0/6.0, don't affects 5.x?

It might affect all of them.

This issue has a workaround: setting the auto-increment key as bigint or unsigned bigint can allow tidb to have a larger key space so that the auto-increment key won't exceed the limit. 

https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/34288 is not sophisticated enough so it was reverted temporarily. We will try to find out a better way to resolve it.

review_comments: maybe log this error, even we may ignore it.
unlike tiflow, tidb repo uses 2 groups on import part. if you're using goland, can set per-project import group setting.
It seems this shouldn't be a noop implemention.

As I concern, `noopTableMetaMgr` is used as long as Lightning is not `local + incremental`. In this sense, Lightning merely allocates rowID from its own memory and needn't reconcile with other instances. So, for `noopTableMetaMgr`, simply returning 0 is trivial and feasible.

What did you suggest to be here?

> allocates rowID from its own memory

We can do this in this method, so that we don't care about the actual implementation on the caller side.

> We can do this in this method, so that we don't care about the actual implementation on the caller side.

It's hard to do so because `noopTableMetaMgr` is somehow a "placeholder" having no idea about the context of the table restoring procedure. If we utilize this contextless structure, we have to:
1. let `singleMgrBuilder` be no longer contextless and maintain a "noopTableMetaMgr" instance.
2. maintain restoring information in `noopTableMetaMgr` (for which, this struct will not be "noop" anymore).

It's good to have a global metadata manager though, I think we should be more circumspect about it and do this change in another PR (to make thing clearer). Maybe I just leave a TODO and file an issue now?
Please add more comments for this method, since `noopTableMetaMgr` doesn't really implement it.
We should handle all possible file types here.

Do we solely support 3 types of source files:
1. csv
2. sql
3. parquet

What else should I handle?
It should be no more. It's better to return an error for unknown file types.
Compared to csv, sql and parquet have some subtle differences. Please check whether we can apply the same algorithm to them.

parquet files won't be sampled in this way. They have provisioned an accurate number of lines.

FYI: https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/0f85650aa43cb60a77ce507e02203db45584e914/br/pkg/lightning/mydump/region.go#L307-L335

I'll handle the unexpected file types then.
